newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt mostly lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt mostly lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mostly lower on Wednesday as customers took profits following the recent rally over the past several weeks, Brady bond traders and market analysts said.
"The market is consolidating. It is taking a breather. We saw some profit-taking in a lot of the assets that had a good run spread-wise," said one trader at a U.S. investment bank.
A drop in the U.S. Treasury market overnight and the dollar following a strong Japanese tankan report added to the softer tone in the Brady bond market, market experts said.
"The Tankan survey came out and that knocked back the dollar and the Treasuries so the Brady market is off with that," said one market analyst.
Among Eastern European credits, Bulgaria suffered the biggest losses on profit-taking but market experts pointed out that the country has been one of the biggest gainers this year.

Bulgarian FLRBs BGFLIRB-RR were 5/8 lower at 55-7/8 bid and discount bonds BGFLTH24A were 5/8 weaker at 55-7/8 bid. Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were 3/8 softer at 91-3/4 bid but prices were still near records highs of 92-7/8 reached earlier this week.

Poland's Brady instruments were only marginally weaker ahead of its Eurobond issue expected on Thursday. The expected $300 million issue will be issued in two tranches, with maturities of seven years and possibly 20 years.
"Poland looks a bit exciting ahead of the bond issue expected tomorrow," said one trader.

In the Latin Brady market, experts said Mexican debt prices were softer on news overnight that the country's international reserves had fallen sharply to $21.258 billion as of June 20, compared to $22.391 on June 13.

"I would say Mexico will probably be the weakest credit in Latin America today," said Richard Gray, emerging market analyst at Bank of America in London. "Two developments in Mexico overnight both of which were a bit negative were the rise in one-month money rates and the expected but nonetheless negative fall in foreign exchange reserves," Gray addded.
